title: Tunable Mediated Interactions Near Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking: From Yukawa to Coulomb and Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya Interactions
abstract: We propose a realization of tunable long-range mediated interactions generated by Nambu-Goldstone (NG) modes near spontaneous symmetry breaking. An effective exchange interaction emerges between two distinguishable impurities proportional to the retarded susceptibility mediated by the bath particles. The interaction is mediated by emergent NG modes associated with symmetry breaking in systems, namely the magnon mode in a repulsive two-component Fermi or Bose gas, or the goldstino mode in a Bose-Fermi mixture. When the NG mode is gapped by explicit symmetry breaking, the interaction has a Yukawa-type short-ranged interaction, whereas the gapless limit gives a Coulomb law. Above the NG mode threshold, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-like cross product coupling emerges in a long-range form. Our proposal paves a way towards the realization of a quantum simulator of spin models and polarons with controllable non-local interactions.
summary: This paper details how tunable, long-range interactions can be engineered between impurities by coupling them to a quantum medium bath near spontaneous symmetry breaking. By controlling the gap of the mediating Nambu-Goldstone mode, the interaction can be tuned between short-range Yukawa, long-range Coulomb, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya forms. This offers a powerful platform for simulating complex spin models using cold atoms.
main_problem: The paper proposes a theoretical framework to realize and characterize tunable, long-range mediated interactions between impurities using Nambu-Goldstone (NG) modes near spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB).
main_result: The mediated interaction can be tuned to exhibit distinct long-range behaviors: Yukawa (gapped), Coulomb (gapless), or oscillatory-Coulomb (Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-like) couplings.
method: The effective interaction is derived by calculating the two-impurity coupling by tracing out the medium bath excitations, utilizing the medium's retarded susceptibility $\chi_{ret}$.
model_or_system: The system involves two distinguishable impurities coupled to a quantum medium bath, which can be realized in various cold atom mixtures, such as Fermi-Fermi, Bose-Bose, or Bose-Fermi mixtures.
key_observables: Effective interaction strength $J(R)$, entanglement entropy, and the phase/amplitude of the interaction, which can be probed via Rabi oscillations or Ramsey interferometry.
important_parameters: The interaction range ($\xi$) and the type of coupling (Yukawa, Coulomb, DM) are controlled by tuning the gap of the NG mode relative to the energy difference between the impurities ($\omega_{	ext{gap}} - \Delta_1 + \Delta_2$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the leading order approximation of the cumulative expansion and uses Random Phase Approximation (RPA) for the itinerant ferromagnetic case.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the three physical systems (Fermi-Fermi, Bose-Bose, Bose-Fermi) and the proposed detection setup using optical tweezers. Figure 2 relates to entanglement entropy measurements.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general Hamiltonian formulation, derives the effective interaction via the medium susceptibility, and then analyzes the resulting interaction structure in different physical regimes (Yukawa, Coulomb, DM) based on the gap tuning.
why_interesting: This work directly connects fundamental concepts of symmetry breaking (NG modes) to controllable, long-range quantum interactions, providing a concrete roadmap for designing quantum simulators using ultracold atomic gases.
